ranking.note: Promoted: silent destruction of valid block data during reindex on supported platforms is the same class of harm as the other P1 crash/data-loss fixes (#36586, #36149).
Raised above other P2s: a node that stays up but can never advance the chain on storage failure is the most consequential non-crash reliability bug here.
Raised: false corruption aborts node startup on pruned/assumeutxo nodes, which is startup-failure territory and close to the P1 group; also unblocks pruneassumevalid work.
Raised to sit next to #36586 and #35003: same family of disk-failure handling, differing only in whether the node aborts or shuts down cleanly.
Raised: corrupt UTXO records silently becoming anyone-can-spend is a fund-safety-adjacent consequence, ahead of the performance P2s.
Raised: largest measured IBD/reindex gain of the performance group (1.15x IBD, 1.53x reindex), so it leads the speedups.
Lowered within P2: speedup depends on unmerged upstream secp256k1 work and is explicitly experimental, so it ranks below the measured, self-contained performance PRs.
Grouped with the other validation performance work; its ~5% IBD gain is smaller than #36000's and #36621's.
Leads the soft-fork group because consensus cleanup also mitigates real timewarp/sigops/Merkle-collision vectors, but still regtest-only so it ranks below active bug and performance work.
Band lowered from P1: identical in nature to #32247/#29247 (regtest-only, no activation, no active defect), so it must share their band.
Kept adjacent to #31989 and #29247; the three regtest-only opcode implementations are of equal consequence.
Placed with the other non-activating opcode implementations rather than above them.
Promoted from P3 and moved up: it fixes a real disk-space leak and is a prerequisite whose commits are included in P2 #36738, so it cannot sit below it.
Moved up to sit immediately after its prerequisite #36735; unblocks kernel pruning tracked in #35627.
Kept P2 as the unblocker of #35570 and the ValidationState cleanup cluster, but ranked below concrete bug/performance work.
Lowered within P2: its own description calls it a minor optimization benefiting mining template checks, well below the node-wide speedups above it.
Lowered: reference implementation explicitly not for merge and vendoring unmerged secp modules, so the decision it enables is further off than for the other soft forks.
Top of P3: it fixes a real cache-population omission in block validity testing and prepares batch validation, unlike the purely structural P3s.
Moved up to sit with the other ValidationState-semantics PRs (#36318, #35646) since they must be reviewed as one cluster.
Moved up: an RPC reporting success after a partially rolled-back chain is a user-visible correctness bug, stronger than the surrounding cleanups.
Moved up to sit beside #36555 and the ValidationState cluster it was discovered in during review of #35570.
Moved up: it is the only assumeutxo PR that adds independent verification of hardcoded commitments, a broader benefit than the operator-recovery fixes below.
Grouped with the other small assumeutxo hardening fixes so they can be reviewed together.
Grouped with #36500 and #36543; all three are narrow assumeutxo robustness fixes of comparable value.
Kept mid-P3: broad compile-time hardening of consensus amount handling, but an RFC draft with no active bug behind it.
Lowered: redundant work and log noise only on a rare invalid-block path, less consequential than the state-correctness P3s above.
Lowered: niche migration for pre-v28 datadirs whose relevance declines over time, below the correctness-oriented P3s.
Lowered: benefit is limited because restarting without -reindex already avoids reprocessing on-disk blocks, making the saved work largely optional.
Lowered: defense-in-depth against hypothetical future script extensions, with no currently reachable ambiguity.
Band lowered to P4: micro-optimization of allocation churn with no benchmarks or profiling, which the definitions explicitly treat as marginal.

inconsistencies: Soft-fork cluster was inconsistent: #31989 (CTV) sat at P1 while #32247 (CSFS), #29247 (CAT), #35793 (BIP 54) and #36122 (CISA) sat at P2 despite all being non-activating, regtest/flag-gated interpreter implementations. All now P2; #35793 first because consensus cleanup also addresses known mainnet attack vectors.
Dependency chain: #36738 includes commits from #36735 and depends on it. #36735 was ranked P3 below its dependent; both are now P2 with #36735 first.
Dependency chain: #35646 removes M_ERROR from ValidationState and is stated to unblock #35570's return-by-value refactor. Review #35646 before #35570.
Dependency chain: #35861 (Testnet 5) is stacked on #35793 (BIP 54) and is in draft awaiting its merge. #35793 must be reviewed first.
Dependency: #35054 (P2P UTXO set sharing) builds on #36603 (loadtxoutset performance pipeline). #36603 first.

Direction conflict: #36598 proposes removing assumeutxo entirely while #36778, #36603, #36543, #36542, #36500 and #35054 all invest in it, and #36346/#36702 fix its crashes. A maintainer decision on #36598 (or a decision that it stays a demo) should precede spending review on the smaller assumeutxo improvements; the crash fixes are needed regardless.

Overlapping scope: #35003, #36049, #34132 and #36280 all change how block/coins I/O and deserialization failures are surfaced (fatal error vs exception vs abort). They touch adjacent code and should be sequenced; #35003 first since it fixes the user-visible stall, then #36049, #34132, #36280.

Overlapping scope: #35751 and #36496 both modify the CoinsViewOverlay parallel prevout-fetch path introduced in #35295; #36496's allocation tuning should land after or alongside #35751's new caller to avoid conflicting assumptions.

Overlapping scope: #35557 (instance clock via ChainstateManager::Now) and #35906 (passing current time explicitly into ContextualCheckBlockHeader) both decouple validation from the process clock by different means; one approach should be chosen.

Cluster around #35904 stateless validation: #35906, #36066 and #35569 are all preparatory steps. They are banded differently (P3/P4/P4) because only #35906 adds testable behavior; reviewers should confirm the overall plan before taking the mechanical ones.
#36702 was found independently during review testing of #36452; both concern startup failures on pruned/assumeutxo chainstates. Review #36702 (crash loop, unbootable) first.
result.notes: The category separates cleanly: P1 is reserved for reproducible crashes, unbootable states, and data destruction (#36586, #36149, #36702, #36346, #35524); P2 holds adversarial-cost and I/O-correctness fixes, measured IBD/startup performance work, and the non-activating soft-fork implementations; P3 is validation-state and cache hygiene plus narrow assumeutxo and perf refinements; P4 is pure structural refactoring and unmeasured micro-optimization. The main global adjustment was flattening the soft-fork group to a single band and lifting #35524 and #36735 to match work of equal or dependent consequence.
